summary: If someone locks his sheep in their pen properly and they get out and do damage, he does not pay. If he did not lock it properly, he pays. If robbers took them out, the robbers pay.

chunks.en: Someone who brings sheep into the pen,
chunks.st: In the case of one who brought his flock of sheep into the pen

chunks.en: and locks the door in front of them properly,
chunks.st: and locked the door before it in a manner that is appropriate,

chunks.en: and they got out and did damage,
chunks.st: and despite this sheep went out and caused damage in another person’s field by eating produce or trampling it,

chunks.en: does not pay. If he did not lock it properly,
chunks.st: the owner is exempt, since he safeguarded the animals appropriately. If he did not lock the door before the sheep in a manner that is appropriate,

chunks.en: and they got out and did damage,
chunks.st: and sheep went out and caused damage,

chunks.he: חַיָּב. נִפְרְצָה בַלַּיְלָה אוֹ שֶׁפְּרָצוּהָ לִסְטִים,
chunks.en: he must pay. If the wall broke at night, or robbers broke it,
chunks.st: the owner is liable, since his negligence led to the damage. If the owner locked the door appropriately but the wall of the pen was breached at night, or bandits breached it,

chunks.en: and they got out and did damage,
chunks.st: and sheep subsequently went out and caused damage by eating or trampling,

chunks.en: he does not pay. If robbers took them out,
chunks.st: the owner of the sheep is exempt from liability. If the bandits themselves took the sheep out of the pen and the animals subsequently caused damage,

chunks.en: the robbers must pay.
chunks.st: the bandits are liable.

summary: More rules about an animal that gets out and eats or ruins things in a garden, and how the damage is measured. Rabbi Shimon says that if it ate ripe food, the owner pays for exactly what it ate.

chunks.en: If he left it in the sun,
chunks.st: If the owner left the animal in the sun, causing it to suffer,

chunks.en: or gave it to a deaf person,
chunks.st: or if he conveyed it to a deaf-mute,

chunks.en: someone not of sound mind, or a child,
chunks.st: an imbecile, or a minor, who are not able to safeguard it,

chunks.en: and it got out and did damage,
chunks.st: and the animal went out and caused damage,

chunks.en: he must pay. If he gave it to a shepherd,
chunks.st: the owner is liable because he was negligent. If the owner conveyed the animal to a shepherd to care for it,

chunks.en: the shepherd takes his place.
chunks.st: the shepherd enters in his place and is responsible for the damage.

chunks.en: If it fell into a garden and got some benefit,
chunks.st: If the animal fell into a garden and derives benefit from produce there,

chunks.en: the owner pays for the benefit it got.
chunks.st: its owner pays for the benefit that it derives and not for other damage caused.

chunks.en: If it went down the usual way and did damage,
chunks.st: If the animal descended into the garden in its usual manner and caused damage there,

chunks.en: he pays for what it damaged.
chunks.st: its owner pays for what it damaged.

chunks.en: How does he pay for what it damaged?
chunks.st: How does the court appraise the value of the damage when the owner pays for what it damaged?

chunks.en: They measure a beis se'ah of that field:
chunks.explain: A beis se'ah is a big piece of land.
chunks.st: The court appraises a large piece of land with an area required for sowing one se’a of seed [beit se’a] in that field, including the garden bed in which the damage took place.

words.note: A beis se'ah is an area where a se'ah of seeds is planted.

chunks.he: כַּמָּה הָיְתָה יָפָה וְכַמָּה הִיא יָפָה.
chunks.en: how much it was worth, and how much it is worth now.
chunks.st: This appraisal includes how much it was worth before the animal damaged it and how much is it worth now, and the owner must pay the difference.
chunks.stMore: The court appraises not only the garden bed that was eaten or trampled, rather the depreciation in value of the bed as part of the surrounding area. This results in a smaller payment, as the damage appears less significant in the context of a larger area.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.he: אָכְלָה פֵּרוֹת גְּמוּרִים מְשַׁלֶּמֶת פֵּרוֹת גְּמוּרִים.
chunks.en: If it ate ripe fruit, he pays for ripe fruit:
chunks.st: This principle of appraisal applies only in a case where the animal ate unripe produce; but if it ate ripe produce, the owner pays the value of the ripe produce.

chunks.en: if a se'ah, a se'ah;
chunks.st: Therefore, if it ate one se’a of produce, he pays for one se’a,

chunks.en: if two se'ah, two se'ah.
chunks.explain: A se'ah is a measure of grain.
chunks.st: and if it ate two se’a, he pays for two se’a.

summary: If someone piles his grain in another person's field without permission, the field owner does not pay if his animal eats it. With permission, he does pay.

chunks.en: Someone who piles grain in the field of
chunks.st: In a case of one who stacks his produce in another’s field

chunks.en: his friend without permission,
chunks.st: without permission from the owner of that field,

chunks.en: and the field owner's animal ate it,
chunks.st: and an animal belonging to the owner of the field eats the produce,

chunks.en: he does not pay. And if it got hurt by them,
chunks.st: the owner of the field is exempt. And if the animal is injured by the produce,

chunks.en: the owner of the pile must pay.
chunks.st: the owner of the stack is liable.

chunks.en: But if he piled it with permission,
chunks.st: But if he stacked them in that field with permission,

chunks.en: the owner of the field must pay.
chunks.st: the owner of the field is liable for damage caused to the produce.

summary: Who must pay for damage done by a fire: the one who sent it, brought the wood, or fanned it. The mishnah also teaches how far a fire can spread before the one who lit it no longer pays.

chunks.en: Someone who sends a fire with a deaf person,
chunks.st: One who sends a fire, i.e., places a burning object, in the hand of a deaf-mute,

chunks.en: someone not of sound mind, or a child,
chunks.st: an imbecile, or a minor

chunks.he: פָּטוּר בְּדִינֵי אָדָם וְחַיָּב בְּדִינֵי שָׁמָיִם.
chunks.en: does not pay in a human beis din, but must answer to Hashem.
chunks.st: is exempt for any damage later caused by the fire according to human laws but liable according to the laws of Heaven.

chunks.en: If he sent it with a person of full understanding,
chunks.st: If he sent it in the hand of a halakhically competent person,

chunks.en: that person must pay.
chunks.st: the halakhically competent person is liable, not the one who sent him.

chunks.en: One brought the fire,
chunks.st: If one person brought the fire,

chunks.en: and one brought the wood:
chunks.st: and one other person subsequently brought the wood, causing the fire to spread,

chunks.en: the one who brought the wood must pay.
chunks.st: the one who brought the wood is liable for any damage caused.

chunks.en: One brought the wood,
chunks.st: Conversely, if one person first brought the wood,

chunks.en: and one brought the fire:
chunks.st: and subsequently one other person brought the fire,

chunks.en: the one who brought the fire must pay.
chunks.st: the one who brought the fire is liable,
chunks.stMore: since it was he who actually kindled the wood.

chunks.en: If another came and fanned it,
chunks.st: If another came and fanned the flame, and as a result the fire spread and caused damage,

chunks.en: the one who fanned it must pay.
chunks.st: the one who fanned it is liable,
chunks.stMore: since he is the proximate cause of the damage.

chunks.en: If the wind fanned it,
chunks.st: If the wind fanned the flames,

chunks.en: none of them pay.
chunks.st: all the people involved are exempt,
chunks.stMore: since none of them actually caused the damage.

chunks.en: Someone who sends out fire and it burned wood,

chunks.st: the one who kindled the fire shall pay compensation” (Exodus 22:5),
chunks.stMore: which teaches that he is liable also for destroying the field itself.

chunks.st: up to what distance may the fire travel within his property for him to still bear liability for damage caused?

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar ben Azaria says:
